Tessa / team — reviewed Novum's request and attached a draft redline (redline_msa_v3.docx) plus a short proposed clause (proposed_training_clause.txt). High-level:

- Blanket opt-out is high-risk for us on hosted/shared models because it limits our ability to improve model safety and degrades long-term product quality. It is more feasible for Dedicated/Private deployments where customer data segregation is already enforced.

- Tradeoffs:
  * If we accept "no use for training" we must also disable telemetry-derived improvements and may need to limit certain automated monitoring features (e.g., anomaly detection that uses aggregated signals). This could increase incident response time and unit cost.
  * We can offer a narrow, contractually-scoped feedback license: non-exclusive, royalty-free, solely for the purpose of debugging and improving the service for Novum's tenant, with aggregation/ de-identification requirements and a 12-month retention cap. For Dedicated customers we can offer a stronger opt-out for cross-customer model training.

- Proposed clause (summary):
  "Customer Data and Customer Outputs. Customer Data and Customer Outputs will remain Customer's property. Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to further train or improve any models trained on or shared across other customers, except as strictly necessary to provide the Service to Customer (e.g., caching, per-tenant performance optimizations). Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated telemetry for internal diagnostic purposes provided no Customer Outputs or Customer Data are reconstructible. Redwood may request permission to use a narrow feedback license limited to debugging and safety fixes; such use requires Customer's prior written consent and will be subject to aggregation and a 12-month retention limit."

- Suggested compromise to present to Novum: (1) Dedicated deployment + contractual "no cross-customer training" commitment, (2) short-term internal diagnostic telemetry permitted under strong de-id rules, (3) optional opt-in feedback license if Novum wants Redwood to use sample outputs for model improvements (explicit consent + data handling controls).

I'm including points for Commercial to present: impact to unit economics if key telemetry features disabled, and a recommended professional services add-on to maintain quality. If Marketing/ Prod want to weigh in on customer experience impact, loop them in.

Dylan
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Claire — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF you sent. We've discussed internally and can offer the following path forward that balances Novum's IP protections with Redwood's operational needs:

1) Option A (Recommended for Dedicated deployments): Contractual commitment that Redwood will not use Novum Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train models used by other customers. The MSA will include the proposed language from our counsel to that effect.

2) Diagnostics: We will retain the right to collect de-identified, aggregated telemetry strictly for diagnostics and platform stability; data reconstructibility will be contractually prohibited.

3) Optional Feedback License: If Novum opts in, a narrow, time-limited feedback license (12 months, non-exclusive, for debugging/safety improvements only) can be added as a separate exhibit, requiring explicit written consent per dataset.

Attached is the proposed clause for your review (proposed_training_clause.txt) and our current redline for the MSA (redline_msa_v3.docx). Could you let me know if Novum's counsel can accept the Dedicated-deployment-first approach? If so, procurement and our deal desk can finalize a Dedicated sizing + pricing exhibit.
